title: Redwood discovery - model selection - DeepSea AI
summary: Initial discovery focused on model selection for a multilingual customer-facing assistant. Customer needs: long context (32k+), tool-calling for internal APIs, and structured outputs for downstream systems. Discussed open model tradeoffs (model size, quantization, context length), routing/fallbacks, latency/cost tradeoffs and next steps to run benchmarks and share security docs.
action_items: Jordan - share model perf spreadsheet and pricing options (hosted/dedicated/private) - due 2027-03-24
Priya - propose benchmark plan and sample prompt set for 32k context + multilingual test - due 2027-03-26
Raj - share infra constraints and security checklist (KMS, VPC, audit log requirements) - due 2027-03-25
Sara - provide representative prompts and language list + tool-call API specs - due 2027-03-24
next_steps: Schedule 1-hour perf benchmark kickoff with Redwood SEs
DeepSea to provide example documents and tool-call API endpoints
Redwood to share SOC2/ISO docs and private deployment architecture notes
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-22 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Alex (Redwood CSM), Liam (CTO, DeepSea), Sara (ML Eng), Raj (Infra), Maya (PM)

00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for blocking time. quick intro, I'm Jordan Miller AE on the Redwood team, with Priya our Solutions Engineer.
00:08 Liam: Hi Jordan, thanks — we've been evaluating folks for the model layer, trying to figure out hosted vs dedic vs private for our customer chat assistant.
00:15 Priya: Great, can you give a quick overview of your use case and must-haves? That'll help us frame model choices.
00:22 Maya: Sure — DeepSea builds a multilingual customer support assistant for shipping logistics. It needs to ingest long manifests, up to 25-40k tokens of context (so 32k is our baseline), call internal APIs for booking lookups, and produce structured outputs for our downstream systems. Also strong support in Spanish, Portuguese, Mandarin.
00:45 Jordan: Got it. So context length, multilingual accuracy, and tool-calling + structured output are primary. Any regulatory or data residency requirements?
00:52 Raj: Yes — some customers in EU require data residency and we have strict PII handling. Ideally private VPC deployment or dedicated capacity with audit logs and KMS integration.
01:05 Priya: Understood. On the model side, broadly there are open models that support long context natively or via context-window tricks, and then there are model size/quantization tradeoffs. For Redwood we support hosted, dedicated GPU pools, and private deployments; we can route requests to smaller/cheaper variants when latency/cost matters.
01:30 Sara: We're specifically looking at open models — want to avoid provider lock-in. But historically we've seen degraded multilingual performance on some smaller open models. We're also curious about tool-calling — how much custom work to enable calling our internal booking API, and how stateful is that across a long conversation?
01:48 Priya: Tool-calling is supported — function-style tool calls with structured JSON outputs are possible, and we can plug into your auth layer. For long conversations we rely on prefix/KV caching to keep recent tokens hot and can stream responses while the model emits tool-call actions. There are nuances though: the larger context windows increase runtime and memory; we may recommend variants with optimized kernels and quantization-friendly execution paths.
02:20 Jordan: Quick question on SLAs — Raj, can you share the team's expectations?
02:26 Raj: We need predictable throughput for peak times — roughly 50 concurrent sessions with 2-4 rps each during peak. Latency target is sub-1.5s for short prompt responses, but for 32k context interactions we can accept higher tail latencies as long as it's predictable.
02:45 Priya: That throughput and predictability maps well to Redwood Dedicated or Private. Hosted can work for MVP but for predictable SLOs, dedicated GPU pools are better. We can also do hybrid routing — critical customers to dedicated, others to hosted.
03:05 Maya: On cost — how do batching and quantization affect cost and latency?
03:12 Priya: Batching reduces per-token compute but can add a small latency buffer; Redwood supports continuous batching with smart scheduling to meet latency SLOs. Quantization (4-bit, 8-bit profiles) can reduce memory and cost — but sometimes at a small accuracy delta, especially for multilingual nuance. We'll recommend a few quantization profiles per model and run regressions on your prompt set.
03:40 Sara: Which open models are you recommending for 32k context and strong multilingual performance?
03:46 Priya: There are a few categories: 1) very large LLMs finetuned for multilingual tasks (often best accuracy but higher cost). 2) long-context models built with special attention patterns (e.g., segmented attention) that scale to 32k. 3) mid-size open models with good performance when paired with retrieval / chunking. For your use case, we usually start with a larger long-context model as a baseline and evaluate trimmed/quantized variants.
04:10 Liam: Any specific names? We've seen references to Mistral long-context forks, and some community patches to Llama-like models.
04:18 Priya: Yep — Mistral forks have good single-token latency and are competitive. There's also models like LongLLM-X (community long-context), and some Redwood-verified variants that we've evaluated. Note: model names are often fuzzy in conversation but main idea is tradeoffs: native 32k support vs chunking + retrieval.
04:40 Jordan: Competitors we've heard about include Anthropic and OpenAI — do you see customers shifting because of accuracy or because of ecosystem features?
04:48 Priya: Customers often pick provider based on operational needs. Anthropic/OpenAI have strong endpoints and fine-tuned models, but open models are attractive for cost and deployment flexibility (private/VPC/on-prem). Redwood aims to bridge that — we give a unified runtime so you can switch model variants or route by policy.
05:05 Raj: About private deployments — what's the control plane model and what needs to stay on-prem?
05:12 Priya: In Redwood Private, the control plane is customer-managed in a VPC; we provide an appliance or k8s Helm chart. Sensitive artifacts like KV cache and model weights stay in your network or in dedicated hardware, and we support KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs. Network egress rules can be enforced. We also have an on-prem installer for air-gapped setups.
05:38 Sara: For tool-calls we need strongly typed outputs — e.g., booking_id, ETA, price_estimate. How do you validate those outputs?
05:45 Priya: We use function/tool schemas and structured output verification in the runtime. You can supply JSON schema for outputs and Redwood will reject non-conforming tool-call results or flag for SE review. We also collect fails and run quality monitoring.
06:05 Maya: Multilingual nuance — Spanish and Portuguese are critical; Mandarin less so but important for some customers. How do you measure regressions when quantizing?
06:14 Priya: We tie quality monitoring to prompt sets and evals — we can run A/B tests, and Redwood Optimize gives regression alerts for languages. We'll run regression checks across your sample prompts when we test quantized profiles.
06:30 Liam: Let's talk performance — can you run a benchmark with our prompts and measure latency/cost across hosted vs dedicated?
06:36 Jordan: Absolutely. Priya can lead the benchmarks. Ideally we'll get a representative prompt set and a list of languages and expected output sizes.
06:45 Priya: Proposed benchmark plan: 1) run baseline on hosted with a large long-context model, 2) run on dedicated with quantized variants, 3) run private if customer wants weights in VPC. We'll measure p50/p95 latency, cost per 1k tokens, and accuracy on your eval set.
07:05 Raj: Anything special needed from our infra? We have firewall restrictions but can open a staging VPC peering or provide a bastion host.
07:12 Priya: For dedicated we need access to push images/config if we host in your cloud; for private we'd work with your infra team to install the control plane. We'll document network ports and provide a checklist.
07:25 Jordan: Quick note on fallback policies — if large model capacity is constrained, we can auto-fallback to a compatible variant and tag responses so you can track quality.
07:34 Sara: For tool-calls and privacy, do logs redact PII automatically?
07:40 Priya: We support token-level redaction rules and audit log controls. We can configure redaction for certain fields; for strict regs we recommend private deployments and retention policies.
07:55 Maya: Timeline — we're aiming for a pilot in 6-8 weeks in EMEA region. Does that sound reasonable?
08:01 Jordan: Yes, with the benchmark and an initial dedicated capacity reservation we can hit that. I'll put options in the email.
08:08 Liam: Good. One more — any known limitations with stateful tool-calls across 32k contexts?
08:13 Priya: Stateful tool-calls are supported but you need to manage the external state store; Redwood helps manage KV cache for tokens but long-term session state should live in your DB, with pointers in the prompt. We'll detail patterns we recommend.
08:30 Jordan: OK let's recap next steps...
08:33 Jordan: Jordan to send pricing and model perf spreadsheet; Priya to propose benchmark plan; DeepSea (Sara/Raj) to share prompts, languages, and infra constraints. Schedule the benchmark kickoff for next week if that works.
08:45 Liam: That works, thanks everyone.
08:48 Meeting end.
